leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling, November 2023 - 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist
leads.documents: Designation of LGBT movement as extremist organization; criminalizes leading, participating, funding, or displaying symbols like rainbow flag; basis for arrests of club owners and fines/jail for symbols
leads.detail: In November 2023, the Supreme Court issued a ruling designating 'the international LGBT public movement' as an extremist group... On 22 March 2024, formally added to the 'unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons' following Ministry of Justice lawsuit

leads.title: Russian federal law, July 2023 - ban on gender transition
leads.documents: Prohibits both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright; bans legal gender change; relevant to transgender legal status and healthcare access
leads.detail: In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition which prohibited both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright

leads.title: Russian federal 'propaganda' law - 2013 law and 2022 expansion
leads.documents: Criminalizes distribution of materials promoting 'non-traditional' sexual relationships; 2022 expanded to all ages and to prohibit materials making minors interested in gender transitions
leads.detail: In 2013, Russia passed a law criminalising distribution of 'propaganda'... in 2022, the 'propaganda' law was expanded to apply to anyone regardless of age group, and to also prohibit distribution of materials that make minors interested in gender transitions

leads.title: Russian federal law, 2024 - adoption ban
leads.documents: Bans adoption of Russian children by citizens/permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions; plus existing rule that couples can adopt only if married heterosexual couple
leads.detail: in 2024 passed a law banning the adoption of Russian children by citizens or permanent residents of countries that allow gender transitions

leads.title: Constitution amendment, July 2020 - same-sex marriage ban
leads.documents: Constitutional ban on same-sex marriage; no same-sex marriages or civil unions allowed; no legal recognition for same-sex relationships
leads.detail: In July 2020, Russian voters approved a Constitution amendment banning same-sex marriage. Neither same-sex marriages nor civil unions of same-sex couples are allowed in Russia

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia, 2021
leads.documents: Ruled it was violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships; Russia left court in 2022
leads.detail: In the 2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg ruled that it was a violation of human rights for Russia not to offer any form of legal recognition to same-sex relationships

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights ruling, 2010 - Moscow Pride / Alexeyev
leads.documents: Fined Russia for discriminating against LGBTQ community after cities systemically refused permits for pride parades; found decisions effectively approved groups calling for disruption
leads.detail: In 2010, the European Court of Human Rights fined Russia for discriminating against the LGBTQ community, after local governments systemically refused to issue permits to pride parades

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report, 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Panel of five expert advisors condemned wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya; documents enforcement via forced disappearances, secret abductions, imprisonment, torture
leads.detail: In a report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council condemned the wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) report, December 2018
leads.documents: Confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons in Chechnya had taken place and was ignored by authorities; follow-up to Novaya Gazeta 1 April 2017 reporting on detentions/torture
leads.detail: A report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons had taken place and was ignored by authorities

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Index 2024 (and 2016)
leads.documents: Institutional ranking of LGBTQ rights status; rated Russia second least LGBTQ-friendly in 2016 and worst out of 49 European countries surveyed in 2024, followed by Turkey and Azerbaijan
leads.detail: In 2016, Russia was rated the second least LGBTQ-friendly nation in Europe by ILGA-Europe. In 2024, the status of LGBTQ rights in Russia was ranked the worst out of the 49 countries surveyed within Europe
